name: Tamsin Hounder
bio: Scour-mistress of the Chalk Hound, as her mother was, and widow of Aldous Hounder, who went down the swallet under Hound Down at the last scouring after a wolf that had come up out of it. She has called the scourers out every seventh summer for forty years. This is the eighth summer since the last, and she has not called them, and the whole Vale is waiting to see if she will.
unique_habit: Ties and unties the white cord round her wrist while she talks, a scourer's knot and back, and never looks at what her hands are doing.

appearance.notes: chalk ground into the knuckles for good, a man's scouring smock cut down, a white cord knotted round the left wrist

schedule.notes: at the gate with the cords, looking up at the Hound

name: Wat Hounder
bio: Tamsin's grandson, fifteen, who has been learning the Scouring Song since he could walk and has never once sung it on the figure. He mends the rakes every day in case today is the day she calls them out.
unique_habit: Hums the Scouring Song under his breath while he works and stops dead at the eye verse, every time, as if somebody had told him not to sing it indoors.

appearance.notes: sleeves rolled, a rake-head in one hand and a mallet in the other, chalk to the elbows

schedule.notes: mending rakes against the day

name: Hedda Limeburner
bio: Keeps Cressbourne's lime kilns above Lime Bay, as her grandmother did. Burns chalk to quicklime for the Vale's cob, its whitewash and its fields, and every spring sends fourteen bushel south to Ashway to lime the headland on the grey side. This spring the cart has not gone, and Rab Ashway has found the grey in his last furrow.
unique_habit: Wipes her hands on her apron and leaves two white prints on whatever she touches next, and does not notice, and the whole Vale knows her handshake by the prints.

appearance.notes: arms white to the elbow with lime, a leather apron burned in spots, eyes red-rimmed from the kiln smoke

schedule.notes: drawing the kilns, before the boars come down the cut at dusk

name: Col Limeburner
bio: Hedda's son, nineteen, who can pick flint out of chalk faster than anybody at the kilns and will not take the south cart past the Hare and Hurdle since a bristleback came at it in spring.
unique_habit: Checks over his shoulder toward the cut every few minutes, and pretends he was looking at the weather.

appearance.notes: a split lip healing, a sling for bristlebacks tucked in his belt that he has never used

schedule.notes: sorting flint by the south cart

name: Oswen Bellsey
bio: Table-Warden of the Brow: keeps the ground of the Long Table between harvests, mends the trestles, writes the places, and rings for the lines that have ended. This spring somebody dug up the Hurdwell bell from the table's foot, and he has rung for an empty hole every evening since.
unique_habit: Rings a small handbell once before he speaks to anybody, very quietly, as if asking the table's permission.

appearance.notes: a handbell on a thong at his belt, a carpenter's pencil behind one ear, trestle-splinters in both hands

schedule.notes: mending trestles and ringing for the lines at the foot

name: Enid Drove
bio: Bramcombe's head shepherd, out on the high down in her wheeled hut from lambing to shearing for forty summers. Counts the ewes into the hurdles twice every evening, and the second count is always one more.
unique_habit: Talks to her crook as if it were a dog, and to her dog as if it were a person who has disappointed her.

appearance.notes: a smock stiff with lanolin, a crook worn smooth to the shape of her hand, a tar-pot on a thong

schedule.notes: on the step with the flock in view

name: Ferris Oakden
bio: A Warden of the Rest, keeping Briarfoot Watch this season with Jessamy Coppin. Thirty years a Warden, twelve of them at gates that do not open. Chalks the tally in a hand like a ledger clerk's.
unique_habit: Rubs out his own chalk marks with his sleeve and writes them again neater when he thinks nobody is looking.

appearance.notes: the Wardens' green-grey cloak, a Warden's bell at the belt, chalk on the right sleeve to the elbow

schedule.notes: at the tally-board, watching the gate

name: Jessamy Coppin
bio: A young Warden on her first season at a gate, keeping Briarfoot with Ferris Oakden. She volunteered for the Briar because she wanted to see the Woodfolk, and has seen three of them at dusk on the far side of the thorn, and they did not wave back.
unique_habit: Waves at the Briar every evening at dusk whether there is anybody there or not.

appearance.notes: a new Warden's cloak too long in the hem, a slate and chalk on a string, a sprig of hawthorn in the brooch

schedule.notes: on the tower stair with the view of the gate

name: Russet Graft
bio: Keeps the Mother Pippin for Tamwick, the tree every apple tree in Wickmere was grafted from. Cuts scions from her every winter and offers them to every farm in the Vale, and for twenty years no farm south of the Hare and Hurdle has taken one.
unique_habit: Carries a grafting knife in his breast pocket and takes it out to look at whenever he is asked a question he has to think about, and puts it away without using it.

appearance.notes: a grafter's apron with pockets full of raffia and wax, green-stained thumbs, a pruning saw on the hip

schedule.notes: tending the Mother before the boars come to the windfalls

name: Linnet Crale
bio: The Wardens' Listener on the Brow: sits at a table outside her shieling on still nights and writes down the singing that comes up from nowhere, under the wind. She has been Listener for eleven years and has three hundred verses, and three blank pages this year, because the three places the singing is loudest are places she cannot bring herself to go at night any more.
unique_habit: Stops mid-sentence to listen, head on one side, whenever the wind drops, and finishes the sentence when it rises again as if nothing happened.

appearance.notes: a Warden's cloak over a shepherd's smock, ink on the fingers, a lantern hook on the shoulder strap

schedule.notes: at the table, listening

name: Bel Axtree
bio: A carter's widow from Tamwick, who buried her husband Tom out on the down in sight of Scathe Fort, with his wheel for a stone, because he would not pay the captain's tithe. She tends the five wheel graves by day and goes back to Tamwick at dusk before the fort's lads come out for the boots.
unique_habit: Straightens each wheel on its grave every morning so the spokes stand the same way, and says the carter's name as she does it.

appearance.notes: her husband's carter's cap, a widow's black band on the sleeve, a spoke-shave in her apron for the wheels

schedule.notes: tending the wheels before the fort's lads come out

name: Abel Larkbourne
bio: The last of the old road crew's line who never went on the road, named for the ganger in the pay-book, living in the one room of the Roadmen's Lodge that still has a roof. The Larkbourne Boys are his grandnephews and great-grandnephews, and they come to his yard once a year to say their own names to the pay-table. He puts the kettle on and does not come out.
unique_habit: Taps the pay-table twice with his knuckle every time he passes it, the way a man greets a horse.

appearance.notes: a road-maker's leather knee pads worn for fifty years, a paviour's rammer used as a walking stick

schedule.notes: sweeping the yard and not talking to the pay-table

name: Garrick Coupler
bio: Kennel-master to the Wardens' Rest, who has bred and run the Rest's nine couple of hounds for thirty years from a line older than the Rest itself. Three nights ago the whole pack went over the kennel wall at midnight without a sound. He chained the gate behind them from the outside and has sat by it since.
unique_habit: Whistles the pack's call under his breath at odd moments, two notes, and then catches himself and stops.

appearance.notes: a kennel-master's horn on a baldric, hound-bites old and white on both forearms, a leash coiled over the shoulder

schedule.notes: by the chained gate

name: Pim Coupler
bio: Garrick's daughter, twelve, who feeds the hounds and names the pups and cannot understand why her father chained the gate against them. She leaves a bowl of scraps outside it every evening.
unique_habit: Calls every hound by name, in order, from Bellmouth to the last pup, every evening at the wall.

appearance.notes: a feed-bucket, a kennel apron much too big, a Warden's bell she was given for her tenth Naming Day

schedule.notes: at the feeding trough with the bowls

name: Tibby Wax
bio: Rookdown's bee-keeper, who keeps the round garth of skeps on the down above the village and tells the bees every piece of news, because bees that are not told leave. She has not told them the grey on the green has reached the well, and she will not.
unique_habit: Speaks to the skeps in a low singsong between sentences to people, so that talking to her is a conversation with three sides, and the bees always get the last word.

appearance.notes: a veil pushed back over a straw hat, wax on the cuffs, a smoker of smouldering rag in one hand

schedule.notes: on the bench by the skeps

name: Coll Ferrant
bio: The Warden keeping Ash Watch this nine days: every keeper is changed on the ninth so that none grows used to the view of the ash and the Choir. He is on his sixth day and has stopped looking south except when he has to.
unique_habit: Keeps his back to the ash while he talks and turns to look at it only at the end of a sentence, quickly, as if checking it has not moved.

appearance.notes: the Wardens' cloak, a flint and steel on a chain for the beacon, a Warden's bell stuffed with wool so it will not ring

schedule.notes: on watch

name: Morwen Dagley
bio: Keeper of Hound Watch, from which a Warden can see the Choir's colossi, the Stair's piers and the whole length of the Vale. She has kept it four years, which is longer than anybody, and the Wardens send her wine, and she knows why.
unique_habit: Raises her mug to the Choir before every drink, as if to an old enemy across a tavern.

appearance.notes: the Wardens' cloak with wine on the hem, a bell-rope wound round one wrist, eyes that look past you to the horizon

schedule.notes: on the crown with the bell

name: Edwy Marl
bio: Keeper of the Brow Beacon, the easternmost fire of the Wardens' line, lit four times in a hundred years and twice this spring. He keeps the wood-stack at nine nights' worth and counts it every morning.
unique_habit: Counts under his breath, always: logs, steps, crows, people, and loses count whenever somebody speaks and starts again.

appearance.notes: a Warden's cloak scorched along the hem, a tinder-box on a thong, sap and soot on both hands

schedule.notes: at the wood-stack

name: Dilly Rookwell
bio: Maud Rookwell's niece, who keeps the fire at the Cliff Hearth on the nights the Rookwells' name comes round on the rota, and on most other nights too, because the other houses forget and she does not.
unique_habit: Feeds the fire one stick at a time with great ceremony and talks to it about whoever it was lit for, as if they were late for supper.

appearance.notes: a shawl smelling of woodsmoke, an armful of hazel sticks, a Rookdown bell on a ribbon at her throat

schedule.notes: keeping the fire into the evening

name: Hale Brakewood
bio: A Woodfolk fletcher sent by the Wold to the Grey End to cut grey thorn, one shaft a day and never from the living side, because the grey thorn makes arrows that do not miss. He is the only fletcher in the Wold who will say out loud what that costs, and still cut it.
unique_habit: Sights along every stick he picks up, even a firewood stick, and puts back the ones that are true.

appearance.notes: Woodfolk leathers patched with Vale wool, a fletcher's bundle of shafts across the back, grey dust in the creases of both hands

schedule.notes: cutting thorn by daylight, gone before the wights come up

name: Emmet Ewell
bio: One of Bram Down's shepherds, living out at the Hurdle Fold from lambing to shearing, who keeps the lambing lantern lit on its crook all night so the ewes know where the fold is in the dark.
unique_habit: Trims the lantern wick every time he passes it, day or night, whether it needs it or not.

appearance.notes: a crook with a lantern hook, a lamb's-tail whistle round the neck, trousers tied at the knee with twine

schedule.notes: with the flock, in before the wolves try the hurdles

name: Mab Dewhurst
bio: The shepherd of Barrow Down's flocks at the Dewpond Fold, from Naming Day to the Long Table. She has watched the dew pond every summer for thirty years and has never once seen it empty or filling.
unique_habit: Glances at the dew pond every time she finishes a sentence, the way somebody else checks a pot on the fire.

appearance.notes: a man's felt hat with a lark's feather in the band, a crook, a leather water-bottle she has never needed to fill

schedule.notes: with the flock at the pond
